name: Shared workbook agent with native and pinned reference frontends W1
order: Alternate native/reference order by block; rotate the four workflows identically. One identical Ready priming job loads each process, followed by declared workflow warmups and measured jobs.
identity: Fresh synthetic workbook per job. A package-internal task-local context freezes fixture UUIDs and dates for paired jobs; both adapters normalize host-generated call IDs. No product environment variable or user setting activates it. Exact prompt arrays and generated tokens are recorded at the actual frontend boundary. Divergent prompts fail the paired-workflow gate. Both generated-token sequences and prompt prefixes must also match; preserve any divergence rather than selectively pairing requests. Compare actual serialized native request frames after normalizing only request ID and deadline stamps; all prompt, sampling, priority, cache-salt, flag and thinking fields must agree.
timing: Complete job includes the actual shared WorkbookAgent loop, all tools, validation/recovery and persisted completion, plus scripted human acceptance/edit/undo for the proposal case. Fixture construction and result assertions are outside timing. Human deliberation time is excluded. Reference uses a development-only private pipe to the pinned Python frontend; pipe/serialization overhead remains included and is separately observable. No HTTP server or product Python dependency. Priming startup is reported separately; OS file caches are uncontrolled.
conditions: Same unchanged engine, verified target/draft bytes, 32K allocation, 12 GiB budget, greedy seed 42, verify-rows all and persistent cache off. Sequential workers; each inference adapter owns the shared model lease. AC power required. No overlapping inference, builds or downloads during a cohort. Native memory includes Swift host/helper; reference includes the same Swift host, Python frontend and helper. Both frontends explicitly use foreground request priority (wire value 0).
sampling: Sample every 0.2 seconds after priming. Record frontend/bridge/helper physical footprints, summed peak, thermal/power/swap before and after. Startup has separate elapsed time and no concurrent-footprint qualification.
exclusions: A lost AC supply, serious/critical thermal pressure or verified external overlapping inference excludes the whole paired block and prevents this fixed-size cohort from qualifying. Preserve all outputs and failures. Swap growth is a finding, not a selective exclusion. Any failed priming, warmup, job, mismatch or sampling failure fails the gate.
pilot: One paired block, one warmup and one measured job per workload/backend. Pilot cannot pass the gate or support speed/adoption claims. Preserve failed pilots; commit the tested harness and protocol before a clean qualifying cohort.
limits: This compares validated workbook jobs with the same host and two frontends, not full UI responsiveness or universal model competence. It does not erase failed R1 raw-model outputs, qualify full occupied 32K/64K contexts, broader hardware or production adoption. Twenty observations per workload/backend are not a population-tail guarantee. Python removal alone establishes no speedup.
